children: Malaysia’s annual inflation rate edged up to 1.9% in August 2026, above the 1.8% market forecast and July’s four-month low, while remaining comfortably within Bank Negara’s 1-1/2%-2-1/2% target range.

Price growth accelerated for food and beverages (1.9% vs 1.8% in July), alcoholic beverages and tobacco (2.8% vs 2.7%), housing (2.1% vs 1.8%), furnishings and household equipment (0.4% vs 0.3%), health (1.3% vs 1.1%), transport (2.0% vs 1.4%), restaurants and accommodation services (2.1% vs 2.0%), and miscellaneous goods and services (3.2% vs 2.9%).

In the meantime, clothing inflation was unchanged at 0.1%, while cost eased for information and communication (2.6% vs 3.4%), recreation and culture (1.1% vs 1.2%), education (1.9% vs 2.0%), and insurance and financial services (1.0% vs 1.1%).
Core inflation fell to 1.7%, its lowest since December 2024, from 1.8% in July.
On a monthly basis, consumer prices rose 0.3%, rebounding from July’s flat reading.

title: Malaysia Inflation Inches Up to 1.9% in August
